timeline.text_full: The trading bot looks healthy overall—status is ok, well within SLA, no errors, and while pnl_90d is negative, that's a performance issue rather than a bug; zero signals acted on is explained by a quiet-market verdict. Now I'm checking coachvision, which shows status ok but is flagged idle, suggesting it hasn't ingested any data yet. Checking coachvision further, it's within its 192-hour SLA at 145 hours, self-test passes with frames processed, no errors — this is expected idle behavior already tracked in existing issues, not a new bug. Now looking at the UFC dashboard, its 7-day success rate is 0.68 across 50 runs, meaning roughly a third are failing, yet last_error is null and the data is fresh with a recent run. I'm weighing whether this failure rate is anomalous or just normal variance from things like API retries, since there's no prior issue tracking this and no explicit error to point to. Digging into the event breakdown, everything looks healthy — no stale events, parse failures, or odds unavailable issues — which makes me lean toward the low success rate being expected scraper flakiness rather than a true regression, especially since there's no baseline to confirm it's dropped from a prior period. The overseer itself looks perfectly healthy: 4 runs, 100% success, no errors, last run 136 hours ago. Since it's a weekly runner and 168h is the full cadence, being 136h out is still within schedule — no staleness flag here. Going through the rest of the week's tools, nothing else stands out as a confirmed bug either — trading is underperforming but error-free, coachvision is idle but passing self-tests, and overseer is clean. The only real question mark left is UFC's 68% success rate over 50 runs, which I want to scrutinize more closely before deciding whether it warrants a filing. timeline.text_full: I'm brainstorming project ideas while checking for duplicates against existing work. For the trading bot, I'm considering a trend chart for signal proximity over time versus just a snapshot, and thinking about per-cluster stop-loss mechanisms since correlated cluster exposure already shipped. For coachvision, since idle escalation is already covered, I'm exploring a custom technique-tagging taxonomy or multi-camera angle merging as fresh directions. For the UFC dashboard, I'm weighing a card confidence score estimating announcement likelihood versus automatic archival of stale event data, since fighter record scraping is already an open item. Then for oversight itself, since proposal quality feedback is already shipped, I'm considering dashboard staleness detection with cache-busting, API cost tracking across projects, or recording implementation diffs in the tracer. Now I'm narrowing toward four or five concrete ideas spanning all repos, starting with a crypto-trading proposal to visualize signal-proximity metric trends over time so regime shifts can be caught before they trigger, and a second one adding a correlated-cluster drawdown circuit breaker that reduces position sizing when groups like BTC/ETH move together past a threshold. I need to differentiate this cluster breaker from the existing correlation guard and rolling risk circuit breaker so it doesn't get flagged as duplicate — the key distinction is a cluster-specific dynamic stop versus the overall Sharpe-based breaker. For coachvision, I'm proposing a configurable technique taxonomy so coaches can tag techniques beyond the default set for multi-discipline support. For the UFC dashboard, I'm considering a heuristic that predicts card-announcement timing based on historical patterns, which is distinct from the existing time-to-event budget allocator since it specifically targets awaiting-card events.
